territorial_scope.description: Applies to data centre projects and bodies in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, with a siting rule for the Horinger data centre cluster.

evidence.quote: 原则上要布局在和林格尔数据中心集群内

summary.short: Inner Mongolia government office opinions (June 2024, valid three years) supporting green computing in the Horinger data center cluster. They set siting rules for large data centres, electricity and green-power measures, network and computing-platform rewards, PUE limits, and innovation and talent support.
summary.long: These government office opinions, issued in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and dated 7 June 2024, aim to support green computing industry development in the Horinger data center cluster. Section 1 provides that new large and super-large data centres (3,000 standard racks or more) should in principle be located in the Horinger cluster, and projects that do not meet the siting requirement do not receive the support policies. Section 2 covers power: coordination of computing, grid and renewable-energy planning; a green-power share of not less than 80%; long-term contracts between renewable generators and computing centres; green direct supply; and renewable quota allocation for projects with at least 10 billion yuan of fixed-asset investment and over 10,000P of computing capacity. Section 3 covers network interconnection and platform incentives: a reward of 10% of platform settlement, up to 2 million yuan per year, for firms connecting to the multi-cloud platform, and a reward of 30%, up to 2 million yuan, for buyers of at least 1 million yuan in annual compute services. Section 4 requires retirement of data centres with annual PUE above 1.5, sets new data centres at PUE 1.2 or below, and encourages low-carbon certification and standards work. Sections 5 and 6 provide a one-off 5 million yuan research grant for newly certified technology centres, talent treatment, and one-off rewards of up to 2 million yuan for projects in national data-element cases, plus pilot demonstration programmes. The text is marked as partially deleted and contains no separate enforcement provisions.

enforcement.note: The text states no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking. Article I(1) provides that projects not meeting the layout requirement do not receive the support policies; this is an eligibility condition and is not coded as a sanction. It is a support measure, so no enforcement regime is recorded.
